3. The facts relevant for determining this appeal may be summarized as follows: The plaintiffs purchased 21 gondas, 3 karas of land by 12 registered deeds from the BS recorded owners, Mohram Ali, Nowhser Ali and Fayez Ahmed and others. While they were holding and possession of the suit lands by mutating their name in BS khatian, the plaintiffs by registered kabala dated 10-2-2003 transferred 10 gondas of land towards the northern side with a specific boundary in favour of the defendant and the remaining 11 gondas, 3 karas lands remained in their possession. The plaintiff No. 1 subsequently transferred 2 gondas, 1 kara lands in favour of the plaintiff Nos. 3 and 4 by different deeds, they are in ejmali possession of their respective lands. The defendant has been possessing beyond 10 gondas of land by force and since there has been quarrel between the parties over the boundary, the plaintiffs are constrained to institute the suit for partition of the lands by metes and bounds. 

 4. The sole defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint stating, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and is barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, Order VII, rule 11 and Order II, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The case of the defendant is that the plaintiffs were the owner of the suit land by way of purchase and while was in possession of the land, transferred 10(ten) gondas of land to the defendant by registered kabala dated 10-2-2005, but it claims that it does not possess beyond 10 gondas land. The defendant after purchase mutated his name in BS khatian and started construction of multi-storied building with the approved plan of CDA, upon taking loan from bank and entered into contract with various persons for sale of apartment from the said 14-storied building. The plaintiffs had no right, title, interest on the said land while purchased by the defendant and as the plaintiffs are not the co-sharers of the said jote the suit for partition is not maintainable and, as such, prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 5. After conclusion of the trial, learned Joint District Judge, Third Court, Chittagong decreed the suit in preliminary form by judgment and decree dated 25-9-2006 to the effect that except 0.20 sataks of land from the Northern side of RS plot No. 639, RS khatian No. 11 corresponding to BS khatian No. 907, BS plot Nos. 1170, 1171, 1172 and 1173 which was sold by the plaintiffs to the defendant, the plaintiffs are entitled to get the rest land. The trial court further directed that— 

 25. To appreciate the point involved, we have perused the entire records. As stated above the suit was decreed in the preliminary form on 25-9-2006 against the sole defendant decreeing the rest of land of RS plot No. 639, RS khatian No. 11 corresponding to BS khatian No. 907, BS plot Nos. 1170/1171/1172 and 1173 excepting 0.2000 sataks of land from the Northern side, which was sold by the plaintiffs to the defendant. The trial court further directed that: 

 After taking delivery, the defendant has been in possession of its purchased land by errecting pucca boundary wall and mutating its name by filing Mutation Case No. 4-0254 of 2003. Accordingly, by order dated 28-3-2003 BS Mutation Khatian No. 907/1 of 2001 (Exhibit- kha) was prepared in its name. In the said BS Khatian, two BS plots i.e. BS plot No. 1170(p), 1171(p), their total share was recorded 0.2000 sataks out of total area of 0.3598 sataks. Although defendant purchased 10 gondas out of RS kbatian No. 639, plot No. 11 (southern side) corresponding to PS Khatian No. 365, PS plot Nos. 25/26/28, corresponding to BS Mutation Khatian No. 907, BS plot Nos. 1170(p), 1171(p), 1172(p) and 1173(p). Since the defendant had been in possession of specific 10 gondas = 0.2000 sataks out of its purchased land, but primarily did not pray for saham in the suit land, as such the plaintiffs are entitled to get saham in the suit by maintaining the boundary of Southern side of the suit plot RS plot No. 11. The Advocate Commissioner submitted his report in conformity with the preliminary decree in as much as, he performed the commission work after serving notice upon the learned Advocates of both the parties. He conducted survey, in presence of the learned Advocates and representatives of both the parties with the help of their surveyors. From the statements of the plaintiffs and the report of the commissioner, written objection of the defendant against the Advocate Commissioner report and the evidence on record, there is no doubt that the final decree has been drawn up in conformity with the preliminary decree. It is worthy to mentioned here that there was no necessity to determine the boundary between RS plot No. 10 and 11, since the land of RS plot No. 10 is no way connected in this suit. To ascertain the suit land, learned Advocate Commissioner fixed RS plot No. 84 as fixed point in presence of the learned Advocate and representatives of both the parties and after taking deposition of the plaintiff No. 1 and defendant's karjakarak and representative, Nurul Islam Khoka (Exhibit-11 series). 

 39. It is worthy to note here that in the present suit preliminary decree was passed on 25.9-2006 and the preliminary decree was made final on 19.2-2012 after rejecting the objection of the defendant against the report of Advocate Commissioner dated 30-9-2009. At this stage of the suit, the defendant long after 9 years filed an application for separate saham on 31-3-2014 disclosing the fact that after purchased the suit land they have mutated their names by opening BS Mutation Khatian No. 907/1 of 2001, creating Municipal holding arid paying rent and taxes to the authority. Defendant then took permissions and approved plan from the CDA on 27-12-2011 for constructing 14-storied residential building in its purchased BS plot Nos. 1170(p) and 1171(p) corresponding to RS plot No. 11(p) and in the meantime constructed 14-storied residential building and sold some flats to different buyers. The plaintiffs filed written objection on 24-4-2014 and additional written objection on 10-9-2014 against the defendants application for saham stating that during pendency of the suit, the defendant out his purchased land sold away 0.0284 sataks land to CDA by registered Kabala No. 18769 dated 8-12-2012 for extension of Hathazari road out of BS plot No. 1170(p) and 1171(p). As such, after sale the defendant now remained owner of 0.899 sataks only but the defendant totally concealed this fact, prayed for saham for entire 10 gondas land.
